notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because none of the sources loaded.

I tried to open six pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Gill, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown and the NET Bible notes. A bug in my code meant I couldn't read what came back. When I tried again, the tool told me I had used up my allowed calls for this turn. So I haven't read a single page on Job 32.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and to leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I've left out everything. I haven't filled any verse from memory.

If you ask again, I'll start fresh and work through:
- **Verse-by-verse sources:** enduringword.com (Job 32), biblehub.com (Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Barnes), studylight.org and preceptaustin.org.
- **Protestant traditions:** sites like gty.org, desiringgod.org, ligonier.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes) and spurgeon.org. I'd look especially at two debated points: whether Elihu is a true spokesman for God or a proud young man, and whether "the breath of the Almighty" in v. 8 means human reason or the Holy Spirit's inspiration.
- **Other views:** netbible.org translator's notes, bibleodyssey.org on the Elihu speeches, and newadvent.org (Church Fathers such as Gregory the Great's *Moralia*). I'd only include popular modern teaching if a site actually discusses it.

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
